institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go to Asia to experience a completely different culture and get some new perspectives. Two of my friends who had gone on exchange in Hong Kong recommended that I go there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The university contacted me and emailed me all the information that I needed. I had a contact person who I could ask for help and she always replied to me within a day or two.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My contact person invited me to an orientation meeting and I was the only MA student in the humanities department. She showed me around the whole campus, helped me get my student ID and answered all my questions. She even had some small gifts prepared for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy but very expensive. My partner got a job in Hong Kong so we lived together and could share the rent. If you are interested in off campus housing you can use the facebook pages "Danskere i Hong Kong" or "Expat Hong Kong". We also used a website to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and small. I lived in Wan Chai which is super central but the university was situated a little over an hour away in public transportation. The public transportation in HK is really good, but that might be too long for some.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My contact person sent me an email with the description if the courses available to me and then I just had to choose five and email them back to her. Then she signed me up for the courses. This was done so that I could choose before the rest of the students and that was very helpful. The course descriptions for the available courses are published quite late around mid-August.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could ask my contact person any questions. She also showed me how to add/drop courses in the system if i wanted to change any of my pre-selected courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful as I could sign up before the other students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just choose the courses that sound interesting to you. After you start you can always change to another course. HKUST use a "shop around" system which means that until mid-September you can go to the first classes of any course and see if you like it. Before you drop a course make sure that there are other available courses and that they aren't full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As an MA student you are not allowed to take any BA courses, but you can join mixed courses. I had two mixed courses where the requirements for the exam were different depending on whether you were a BA or an MA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar to UCPH, as many of the professors were educated from US universities. However, they used a lot of Chinese sources and ideas. There was a greater focus on grades than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Politcal Culture, Fascism, History and the Future, Images of Japan, Animals and Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In Political Culture I had a great professor who really understood how to get the best out of her students. She used new and relevant studies to teach us about how to measure culture and she was not afraid to talk about sensitive political topics even in a room filled with mainland Chinese students and local Hong Kong students. In Animals and Society I was given a new perspective on societies view on animals. It was incredibly interesting and I learned about so many new perspectives on medicine, covid-19 and global warming.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I anticipated. You can get cheaper food than I did, but it will take some planning. Public transport is subsidised and you can get money back every month by using these machines at the big stations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They arranged barbecues, Christmas dinner, hikes and culture walks with food. You could join a kayaking class and other water sports activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really join in any of the cultural activities, so I can't say. This was probably a side-effect of living off campus, but I did get emails about activities I could join I just didn't. Other students told me the sailing club was really fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are so many things to do in Hong Kong. Go to Sai Kung on a hike and visit the beautiful pier. Go to the many beautiful Islands. Go on a Junk boat to meet new friends, swim and party. Go to Sham Shui Po and visit the huge market! (Remember to bring cash). Go to central and take the mid-levels escalators to Tai Kwun to sit on the square of the old prison. Visit Macau's old town, eat the traditional almond = cakes, dragon beard candy and the delicious egg tarts. Bring your friends out for Yum Cha and eat traditional Dim Sum. Eat the best food in the world! There are endless things to do and see in HK.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with them in between classes and in the breaks. People are very friendly but they also have their own friends, so be proactive and ask them to eat lunch together or hang out. I was approach by many people to talk and connect. Although, most people that approach you are probably exchange students themselves, some are local. The Mainland Chinese students are the most interested in you in my experience. People share their snacks and ask about your country.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't find any differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food! The friendly people and language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Ebneezer's Kebab is the best for lunch
There's a shuttle bus from campus to the big areas of HK - use it, it is free!
The security guards will help you if you are lost

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a sweater because it might be hot outside but inside is super cold. People wear masks when they are sick, but still come to class. The professors are very helpful so write them with any questions you have. Enjoy!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to discuss current topics with students that have completely different reference points and knowledge than you.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finishing my exams on time as we only had one week off before they were due.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
